title: Candles
hookLine: a candle as a prayer that keeps burning when you leave

cards: Near the side wall of a church, a stand of small candles. Some burning, some burned down to wax, some new. A man comes in on his lunch break, still in his work jacket.
He drops a coin in the box, takes a fresh candle, lights it from one already burning, and sets it in its place. He stands a moment. Then he checks the time and goes back out into the noise.
The candle doesn't go with him. It keeps burning in the quiet church, for whoever he lit it for, after he's back at his desk. Today: candles.

teach.b: For the people who light one, a candle in church does something a spoken prayer can't: it keeps going when they stop. Start with light itself: "Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path."
In the psalm, light lets you take the next step.

And Jesus says, as on day one hundred seventy-three, that a light is meant to be seen: "Neither do men light a candle, and put it under a bushel, but on a candlestick; and it giveth light unto all that are in the house."
A candle on a stand is that sentence, burning. Next, a fire that stays lit.

teach.h: THE FIRE SHALL NEVER GO OUT.
teach.b: In Leviticus, the priests are told: "The fire shall ever be burning upon the altar; it shall never go out." Then, prayer that doesn't stop.
Paul tells the church in Thessalonica, "Pray without ceasing."

So some Christians, Orthodox and Catholic among them, light a candle before an icon or a statue, for someone who is sick, someone far away, someone who has died, and say that the flame goes on praying after they've walked out the door.
Other churches light candles in their own ways, on an Advent wreath or held in the hand on Christmas Eve. Last, the person.

teach.h: THE SPIRIT OF MAN IS THE CANDLE OF THE LORD.
teach.b: Proverbs goes further: "The spirit of man is the candle of the LORD." In that picture, a candle isn't only something a person lights. A person is one.
So the small flame on the stand is lit by someone, for someone.

how: In Orthodox and Catholic churches people light small candles before icons and statues for the living and the dead and leave them burning; other churches light candles on an Advent wreath or hold them at candlelight services.

o: a light lit only to brighten a dark church
a flame lit for someone, burning after you leave
a flame that must burn before any prayer counts

p: the fire shall never go out

s: people light candles in some churches and leave them burning after they go
the flame stands for someone, and goes on after the person who lit it has gone.
Jesus says a lit candle belongs under a bushel
the opposite: "on a candlestick; and it giveth light unto all that are in the house."

games.q: on your lunch break you've lit a candle in a quiet church for someone you love. it's time to go back to work. what do you do with the candle?
o: blow it out before you leave
stay until it burns all the way down
games.why: people leave it burning: a prayer that goes on after they've walked out the door.

practice: If you have a candle and it's safe, light it where you can see it; if not, turn on a small lamp or any light near you.

Bring one person to mind, someone you love, someone struggling, someone you miss, and let the flame stand for them. If you pray, hold them in your prayer while you watch it; if you don't, keep them in mind, as steady as the flame.

wordCard.voice: Candles. Small flames lit in churches for someone, living or dead, so a prayer can go on burning after whoever lit it has gone.

orig.note: Greek: lamp, the word the King James renders "candle" in Matthew 5:15.

carryVoice: Your line: a prayer left burning. It stays lit when you go. See you tomorrow.
